evidence_snippets: “Six different serotypes have been identified based on the serological specificities of their polysaccharide capsules, with capsular serotype b as the predominant strain associated with invasive H. influenzae disease. Strains without capsules are referred to as non-typeable.”
“Vaccination against H. influenzae serotype b (Hib) was introduced in the 1980s…”

“In theory, vaccines that target only one serotype may drive the organism to either switch and/or replace their capsules with nonvaccine capsular types or shed their capsule altogether to become resistant to the vaccine.”
key_data_points: Hib vaccine targets Haemophilus influenzae serotype b only (serotype-specific coverage).
Haemophilus influenzae has six capsular serotypes (a–f); non-typeable strains lack capsule.
study_population: Invasive Haemophilus influenzae cases in British Columbia, Canada (2008–2009), children and adults (98 cases total)

Infants/children in head-to-head studies of licensed hexavalent vaccines (multiple countries including Colombia, Costa Rica, Mexico, Thailand, Germany, Czech Republic, Sweden, Finland, Belgium, Italy).

evidence_snippets: Hexaxim® is fully liquid, hexavalent, combination vaccine that provides immunization against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis (whooping cough), polio, hepatitis B, and invasive diseases caused by Haemophilus influenzae type b.
Haemophilus influenzae type b polysaccharide: (Polyribosylribitol phosphate) 12 μg (Conjugated to Tetanus protein 22–36 μg).
Hexaxim contains diphtheria, tetanus, acellular pertussis (aP), inactivated poliovirus (IPV), HB, and Hib (purified capsular polysaccharide conjugated to tetanus toxoid [PRP~T]) antigens.
key_data_points: Hib serotype coverage: Haemophilus influenzae type b (PRP~T conjugate).
study_population: Infants/toddlers across >25 clinical trials (approximately 7200 infants/toddlers) in multiple countries (e.g., South Africa, India, Turkey, Germany/Czech Republic, Vietnam, Finland, Mexico/Peru, Argentina, Thailand, Colombia/Costa Rica, South Korea, Spain, Russian Federation).

evidence_snippets: “DTaP-IPV-HB-PRP-T or hexavalent vaccines are indicated for primary and booster vaccination of infants and toddlers against diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, hepatitis B, poliomyelitis and invasive diseases caused by Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib).”

“Each dose (0.5 mL) of MenC vaccine (NeisVac-C®, Baxter A.G.; batch number: VNSM04C) contained: 10 μg Neisseria meningitidis serogroup C polysaccharide conjugated to 10--20 μg tetanus toxoid; and 0.5 mg aluminium hydroxide…”

“Since the introduction of meningococcal serogroup C conjugate (MenC) vaccines in the national immunisation programmes for infants and toddlers, there has been a substantial decline in invasive meningococcal disease (IMD) caused by serogroup C.”
key_data_points: Hexavalent DTaP-IPV-HB-PRP-T targets: diphtheria, tetanus, pertussis, hepatitis B, poliomyelitis (types 1, 2, 3), and Haemophilus influenzae type b (Hib).
Co-administered meningococcal vaccine is serogroup-specific: Neisseria meningitidis serogroup C (MenC).
study_population: Healthy full-term infants in Finland aged 46–74 days at enrollment (randomized n=350).

evidence_snippets: “Encapsulated strains are classified according to the chemical composition of the polysaccharide capsule. Six serotypes, types a, b, c, d, e and f, have been identified. Of these, serotype b is responsible for approximately 95% of all invasive disease serotypes with Haemophilus influenzae.”

“The observation that the low incidence of Hib disease in older children and adults correlated with the presence in their serum of bactericidal antibodies directed against the Hib capsular polysaccharide, PRP, led to development of a vaccine based on the type b capsular polysaccharide alone.”
“The Hib capsule is composed of repeating polymers of ribosyl and ribitol-phosphate (PRP)…”
key_data_points: Haemophilus influenzae has six encapsulated serotypes: a, b, c, d, e, f
Serotype b accounts for ~95% of invasive Haemophilus influenzae disease
Hib vaccines target the type b capsular polysaccharide (PRP)
study_population: Not applicable (WHO position paper / global guidance; not a single study population)

evidence_snippets: Poliomyelitis (polio) is a highly contagious acute disease caused by one of three poliovirus serotypes (poliovirus types 1, 2, or 3).
In 2016, there was a globally synchronized "switch" to replace trivalent oral poliovirus vaccine (tOPV) with bivalent oral poliovirus vaccine (bOPV) containing only types 1 and 3.
Trivalent OPV (tOPV, containing types 1, 2 and 3) was licensed in 1963, and bivalent OPV (bOPV, containing types 1 and 3) in 2009.
Sabin OPV was first licenced as monovalent OPV (mOPV, containing type 1, 2 or 3) in 1961
IPV is given by injection and is commercially available only in trivalent form containing the 3 virus serotypes, PV1, PV2 and PV3.
The 2 doses of IPV provide immunity against paralysis from type 2 poliovirus and also boost immunity against poliovirus types 1 and 3.
key_data_points: mOPV serotype coverage: monovalent type 1 or type 2 or type 3
IPV serotype coverage: PV1, PV2 and PV3 (trivalent only)
study_population: Not applicable (WHO position paper; not a single study population)
